summary: The bill amends the Animal Welfare Act to ban commercial greyhound racing, live-lure training, and open-field coursing by making it illegal to conduct or facilitate such events (or betting on them) when greyhounds move in interstate commerce, to use live animals as bait, or to buy, sell, train, or transport greyhounds for these purposes, with fines and up to seven years in prison, effective October 2027.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It focuses solely on amending the Animal Welfare Act to prohibit certain activities involving greyhounds.
No references to taxes, tax policy, rates, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare systems, coverage, or medical policy in any way.
There is no content related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill makes no mention of immigration, borders, visas, or related policies.
No provisions or findings address reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill has zero connection to military or defense spending or policy.

While the bill protects animals, it does not engage with environmental regulations, climate policy, pollution controls, or land use protections. Animal welfare under the Animal Welfare Act is distinct from broader environmental topics.
No elements relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
The bill contains nothing about schools, education funding, or school choice.
Findings reference drug testing of greyhounds but create no new drug policy, enforcement, or decriminalization measures.

The bill adds new federal criminal prohibitions with penalties of fines and up to 7 years imprisonment per violation. This represents a modest expansion of federal criminal law and enforcement authority in a narrow area, though it is not the bill's primary focus.
No provisions address trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export policy beyond incidental references to interstate commerce in the context of animal transport.
The legislation has no implications for deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content relates to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not mention foreign aid or international assistance programs.
There are no provisions concerning voting rights, elections, or election integrity.
References to simulcast betting and internet communications are incidental to defining prohibited activities and do not regulate technology, data privacy, or tech oversight.
The bill has no bearing on labor rights, unions, or employment policy.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil rights, or discrimination policy.
